About
UN Open Source Week 2026

UN Open Source Week 2026 is the premier global forum for advancing open source collaboration in direct support of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Global Digital Compact. The event demonstrates how open source drives digital cooperation, fosters innovation, and enables sustainable public infrastructure, turning ideas into practical impact.

Through panels, workshops, hackathons, and community-led events, participants will connect to discuss real-world solutions and gain actionable insights in topics such as artificial intelligence (AI), Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) and Open Source Program Offices (OSPOs).

UN Member States, agencies, private sector organizations, civil society, and technical communities will gather to bridge the gap between high-level policy and practical implementation.

Co-Organizers

UN Open Source Week is co-organized by leading UN entities driving digital innovation and collaboration.

Co-Organizers

United Nations Office for Digital and Emerging Technologies (ODET)

ODET was established by the General Assembly on 1 January 2025 to advance inclusive, rights-based and multi-stakeholder digital cooperation that respects national priorities and contexts. It also serves as the United Nations system-wide focal point for digital issues. It operates under the following strategic functions: (1) Advise Senior Leadership on Technology Trends; (2) Advocate for Digital Cooperation; (3) Faciltiate Multi-Stakeholder Policy Dialogue; (4) Strengthen System-Wide Coordination; (5) Support the Global Digital Compact (GDC).
Co-Organizers

United Nations Office of Information and Communications Technology (OICT)

The Office of Information and Communications Technology (OICT) enables a better, safer, more sustainable future through innovative technology. OICT is responsible for defining strategic direction for ICT in the Secretariat. It provides oversight of ICT programmes, systems, applications and decision-making. The office is committed to ensuring colleagues all over the world have the necessary ICT tools to succeed in their respective mandates.

UN Tech Over

The UN Tech Over brings people together to work on real UN challenges and build practical solutions. This day will be about moving from discussion to action, proving that open source can turn global goals into real tools. This event will demonstrate how open source collaboration can help translate global priorities into practical, reusable tools, and support ongoing efforts toward the implementation of the Global Digital Compact.

LinkedIn Side Event Description
LinkedIn Office

This invite-only event is hosted in collaboration with LinkedIn, bringing together select participants to discuss and explore key topics related to the impact of artificial intelligence in the workforce.

Open Source for AI and Emerging Technologies
UN headquarters

Open Source for AI and Emerging Technologies (Open Source x AI) assesses the potential of open source as a gateway to establishing a sustainable AI future. Through the examination of topics such as open hardware and open robots, the Day aims to bridge digital divides, promote responsible AI development, and build AI capacity.

DPI Day
UN headquarters

This event positions Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) as a critical enabler of the digital economy and broader digital transformation. By aligning operational strategies with national priorities, DPI Day promotes the inclusive design, implementation, and long-term sustainability of DPI projects. Participants will discuss how to translate the commitments made in the Global Digital Compact, which include investments in DPI and Safeguards, into concrete action.

OSPOs for Good
UN headquarters

OSPOs for Good to showcase the value of Open Source Program Offices (OSPOs) in advancing sustainable development and digital transformation. Through panels, case studies, and expert discussions, the event highlights best practices to accelerate open source adoption across UN agencies, governments, and private sector institutions. OSPOs for Good will mobilize the open source ecosystem to drive capacity building and global knowledge sharing.

Community-Led Events
IBM One Madison

The Community-Led Side Events will showcase community-driven projects, facilitate knowledge exchange, and encourage collaboration across sectors. Participants engage in workshops, presentations, and discussions that demonstrate the impact of open source initiatives in supporting digital cooperation and inclusive innovation.

Chief Executive Officer, Opendata.ch

Dr. Verena Kontschieder is a policy and technology governance expert. She holds over a decade of experience in shaping global approaches to AI and digital governance across leading industry, government, and multilateral institutions, such as the World Economic Forum, European Commission, World Bank, IMF, and African Development Bank.

At Meta, she launched and scaled Open Loop, an award-winning global program that pioneered experimental, human-centric design-led multi-stakeholder approaches to AI governance. 

Verena currently directs the Prototype Fund Switzerland and is CEO of Opendata.ch, supporting public-interest technology and responsible digital and data innovation. She also works in strategic innovation and advisory board positions at startups and international initiatives that aim at bridging AI and humanity. She holds a PhD from the Royal College of Art, London, where her research focused on human-centric approaches and public value creation in global AI and technology governance.

Kanono Ramashamole

Principal Secretary, Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation (MICSTI), Kingdom of Lesotho

Mr. Kanono Ramashamole serves as Principal Secretary of the Ministry of Information, Communications, Science, Technology and Innovation of the Kingdom of Lesotho, where he leads the Ministry's strategic direction across digital governance, information and communications technology policy, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence, and the national digital transformation agenda. As the Ministry's chief accounting officer and senior negotiator, he oversees both domestic policy implementation and Lesotho's engagement in international digital governance fora.

He chairs the Universal Service Fund Board of Trustees and represents Lesotho across the African Union, the International Telecommunication Union, the United Nations system, and the Southern African Development Community on matters of digital governance, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence policy, and Digital Public Infrastructure.

A consistent advocate for inclusive and rights-based Digital Public Infrastructure, Mr. Ramashamole has championed the integration of safeguards for children within national DPI design, aligning Lesotho's efforts with the 50-in-5 DPI Campaign, the Smart Africa Alliance, and UNICEF's DPI Safeguards for Children. His work emphasises foundational digital identity, interoperability, and data protection frameworks that are secure, equitable, and protective of vulnerable populations.

Mr. Ramashamole holds a Bachelor of Science in Mathematics and Physics and a Bachelor of Science in Electrical Engineering (Light Current). He combines deep technical expertise as an active software developer with senior public-service leadership at the intersection of national and international digital governance.

Making DPI Work for Children: From Country Experience to Implementer Tactics

24 June
 
15:00
 - 
16:00
Speakers
Speaker details will be announced soon.

About the Session

Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI) is increasingly becoming the backbone of public service delivery, and the decisions made at the infrastructure level will define children's access to health, education, and social protection. Access to birth registration, health care, school enrolment, and social protection depends not on any single system, but on the ability of multiple government agencies to share data securely and reliably across administrative boundaries. 

Yet experience shows that children's specific needs, rights, and risk profiles are rarely made explicit at the DPI design stage. When this happens, DPI can unintentionally reinforce fragmentation, exclusion, or gaps in safeguards, despite strong intentions to improve efficiency and integration. 

This session examines what makes DPI work for child rights in practice, from the core building blocks and safeguards to the implementation realities and governments’ choices that shape outcomes for children across health, education and social protection. 

Pairing high-level country testimony with implementer-level tactics and insight from CDPI's advisory experience across national DPI deployments and UNICEF’s global perspective on child rights, the session surfaces operational gaps, institutional dynamics, and the speed-vs-safeguards trade-off that shape outcomes for children.

It aims to: 

  • Identify the DPI building blocks that are most critical for inclusive service delivery for children
  • Draw out country-level lessons that can advance better design and decisions on DPI
  • Explore practical implementation and deployment approaches, including rapid deployment, operational models, resourcing and pathways from pilot to scale
  • Examine the legal, technical, and institutional safeguards needed to protect child rights at the infrastructure level; and
  • Consolidate field-tested implementer tactics and a potential roadmap to develop DPI around an agreed child-centred public problem (e.g. ensuring every child is counted and continuously served from birth registration through school enrolment to social protection)

Partners: Dominican Republic, UNICEF, Centre for Digital Public Infrastructure (CDPI)

Ahunna Eziakonwa

Assistant Secretary-General and UNDP Regional Director for Africa, UNDP

Ms. Ahunna Eziakonwa is a global development leader and dedicated Afro-optimist who champions African agency, innovation, and leadership. As UNDP’s Regional Director for Africa, she oversees operations in 46 countries and manages a $1.2 billion development portfolio. She leads bold initiatives like timbuktoo, UNDP’s flagship effort to build Africa’s startup ecosystem, and the African Influencers for Development platform, mobilizing leading African voices for sustainable change. A steadfast advocate for youth and women, she spearheaded the Africa Facility to Support Women in Political Leadership and launched the African Young Women Leaders Fellowship Programme, empowering over 96 young African women across the UN system. Advancing resilience and inclusive governance, she established the Africa Facility for Inclusive Transitions to promote African-led transitions and national ownership, and shaped the UNDP Africa Borderlands Initiative and #IAMSAHEL campaign to tackle fragility through investment and resilience. She also drives economic transformation through Africa’s Money for Africa’s Development agenda and systemic reforms like the Credit Rating Initiative. She previously served as UN Resident Coordinator and UNDP Resident Representative in Ethiopia, Uganda, and Lesotho. She is a graduate of Columbia University’s School of International and Public Affairs, she also holds a Bachelor’s in Education from the University of Benin, Nigeria, and has completed executive programs at the Harvard Kennedy School.

Yann LeCun

Executive Chairman of Advanced Machine Intelligence (AMI Labs); Jacob T. Schwartz Chaired Professor of Computer Science at New York University (NYU)

Yann LeCun is the Executive Chairman of AMI Labs and the Jacob T. Schwartz Professor at NYU affiliated with the Courant Institute - School of Mathematics, Computer Science, and Data Science. He was the Chief AI Scientist at Meta (2018-2025), the founding Director of Meta-FAIR (2013-2017), and of the NYU Center for Data Science (2011-2014). He received an Engineering Diploma from ESIEE (Paris) and a PhD from Sorbonne Université (1987). After a postdoc in Toronto he joined AT&T Bell Labs in 1988, and AT&T Labs in 1996 as Head of Image Processing Research. He joined NYU as a professor in 2003 and Meta/Facebook in 2013. His interests include AI, machine learning, computer perception, robotics, and computational neuroscience. He is the recipient of the 2018 ACM Turing Award (with Geoffrey Hinton and Yoshua Bengio) for "conceptual and engineering breakthroughs that have made deep neural networks a critical component of computing", a member of the National Academy of Sciences, the National Academy of Engineering, the French Académie des Sciences.

Hon. Amb. Audrey Marks

Minister of Efficiency, Innovation and Digital Transformation, Office of the Prime Minister, Jamaica

The Honourable Ambassador Audrey Marks is Minister of Efficiency, Innovation and Digital Transformation in the Office of the Prime Minister.

Minister Audrey Marks had previously served as Jamaica’s Ambassador to the United States and Permanent Representative to the Organization of American States. She holds the historic honour of being Jamaica’s first female Ambassador to the United States, and is the only person to have held the post three times, across four administrations.

Ambassador Marks’s work in strengthening Jamaica - U.S. bilateral relations and championing Jamaica’s interests at the OAS has been widely respected and impactful.

After demitting the office of Ambassador to the USA, she was appointed a Senator in Jamaica’s Parliament and a Cabinet Minister in March 2025. On 3rd September 2025, she successfully contested in the country’s General Elections and was elected as the first female Member of Parliament for the Manchester North Eastern Constituency.

Minister Marks is also a pioneering entrepreneur who transformed Jamaica’s financial landscape as the founder of Paymaster (Jamaica) Limited - one of the first companies in the world to offer internet-based, multi-transaction payment systems. Her business portfolio has spanned agriculture, transportation, real estate, and more, earning her recognition as an innovator and entrepreneur extraordinaire both locally and internationally.

She holds a Bachelor of Business Administration from the University of the West Indies and an MBA from Nova Southeastern University in Florida. Her commitment to public and private sector development has seen her serve on over 20 national and international boards, including becoming the first female President of the American Chamber of Commerce of Jamaica.

In recognition of her remarkable contributions, she has been awarded the national honour of The Order of Jamaica (OJ). Minister Marks has also received honorary Doctor of Laws degrees from both the University of the West Indies and the Northern Caribbean University.

Now, as Minister of Efficiency, Innovation & Digital Transformation, Ambassador Marks has been charged with the responsibility to drive Jamaica’s economic growth agenda by reforming the country’s bureaucracy and becoming a technologically enabled society. Her signature goal is to implement the government’s SPEED Program (i.e., Streamlining Processes for Efficiency and Economic Development) to shape policy, drive productivity, and ease of doing business in the country, while inspiring the next generation of Jamaican innovators.

Frederik Blachetta

Chief Technology Officer, Bundesdruckerei Group

Frederik Blachetta has been a member of the Executive Management of Bundesdruckerei Gruppe GmbH since mid-February 2026, both as Chief Technology, Data & Innovation Officer (CTO) and as Managing Director of Bundesdruckerei GmbH. Blachetta has many years of leadership and transformation experience in the digitalisation of public administration. As a Partner at PwC, he was Global Public Sector Data & AI Leader and was responsible for international digitalisation, data and AI programmes in the public sector. Prior to that, as the first Chief Data Officer at the Federal Chancellery, he set up and led the Federal Government’s data and AI labs and at Dataport, he drove forward strategic transformation as Chief Strategy Officer. Blachetta holds a Bachelor of Science degree in economics from Freie Universität Berlin and subsequently earned a Master of Laws from Goethe University Frankfurt.

Kush R. Varshney

IBM Fellow, IBM Research

Kush R. Varshney is an IBM Fellow and a leader in human-centered trustworthy AI, renowned for his work in integrating algorithmic fairness and transparency into complex enterprise systems. Through his leadership of the IBM Science for Social Good initiative and the creation of foundational open-source offerings like AI Fairness 360 and Granite Guardian, he has consistently demonstrated how collaborative ecosystems can operationalize responsible AI at scale. Dr. Varshney bridges the gap between theoretical research and practical, impactful deployment to advance the global AI commons for the benefit of society. He published the book Trustworthy Machine Learning in 2022.

Jim Zemlin

Chief Executive Officer, Linux Foundation

Jim Zemlin is the CEO of the Linux Foundation, the world’s leading organization for open source software, standards, and collaborative innovation. He works with many of the world’s largest technology companies—including Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, IBM, NVIDIA, Samsung, Qualcomm, and others—to help shape the future of artificial intelligence, cloud computing, and digital infrastructure.

Under his leadership, the Linux Foundation has grown into one of the most influential technology organizations in the world, serving as the home for many of the industry’s most important shared technology investments, including Linux, Kubernetes, PyTorch, MCP and RISC-V. Through its global ecosystem of companies, developers, and research institutions, the Linux Foundation enables collaborative innovation at a scale unmatched in the technology industry.

Zemlin’s career has spanned the rise of open source, cloud computing, and AI, and he is widely recognized for his insights into technology strategy, innovation, and the economics of the digital industry. A frequent keynote speaker, he advises technology leaders, startups, governments, and nonprofit organizations around the world on the future of computing and open collaboration.

Mostafa Elkordy

Senior Cybersecurity Solutions Officer, UNICC

Mostafa Elkordy brings over two decades of hands-on experience in software architecture and large-scale system development, with a focus on secure, interoperable, and resilient digital systems in complex international environments. His work spans enterprise integration, identity and access management, and security assurance, including adversarial validation and penetration testing of large-scale systems. He currently serves as Senior Cybersecurity Solutions Officer at UNICC and as Chair of Open Source United, a Community of Practice within the United Nations ecosystem.

He has led initiatives in secure platform engineering and digital trust, with a strong emphasis on practical approaches to cybersecurity, system resilience, and cross-organizational interoperability.

He is also the founding author of OSARA (Open Sovereign Agent Reference Architecture) and its companion AI Bill of Rights, an emerging open framework intended to provide holistic guidance on how individuals, enterprises, and governments can interact through AI agents in a sovereign, secure, and interoperable manner. The work also explores broader implications for the future of work, as well as the regulatory and governance considerations required to support agent-driven digital ecosystems.

‍
